sanskrit: ātmeva veditavyeṣu priyeṣv iva ca jīvitam itihāsaḥ pradhānārthaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvāgameṣv ayam
english: Just as the self is the most worthy of all things to be known, and life the most dear of all beloved things, so this history is the foremost in purpose and the greatest among all scriptural traditions.

sanskrit: itihāsottame hy asminn arpitā buddhir uttamā svaravyañjanayoḥ kṛtsnā lokavedāśrayeva vāk
english: In this supreme history, the finest intellect has been employed; the entire range of vowels and consonants, all speech rooted in the world and the Veda, finds its home here.

sanskrit: asya prajñābhipannasya vicitrapadaparvaṇaḥ bhāratasyetihāsasya śrūyatāṃ parvasaṃgrahaḥ
english: Of this history of the Bhāratas, rich in wisdom, adorned with varied words and divisions, let the summary of the parvas now be heard.

sanskrit: parvānukramaṇī pūrvaṃ dvitīyaṃ parvasaṃgrahaḥ pauṣyaṃ paulomam āstīkam ādivaṃśāvatāraṇam
english: First comes the Index of Parvas; second, the Parva-Compendium; then the Pauṣya, the Pauloma, the Āstīka, and the Descent of the Primeval Lineage.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃbhavaparvoktam adbhutaṃ devanirmitam dāho jatugṛhasyātra haiḍimbaṃ parva cocyate
english: Then is recounted the Sambhava Parva, wondrous and fashioned by the gods; within it is the burning of the house of lac, and the Hiḍimba Parva is also told.

sanskrit: tato bakavadhaḥ parva parva caitrarathaṃ tataḥ tataḥ svayaṃvaraṃ devyāḥ pāñcālyāḥ parva cocyate
english: Then the parva of the slaying of Baka; then the Citraratha Parva; and then is told the parva of the svayamvara of the princess of Pāñcāla.

sanskrit: kṣatradharmeṇa nirjitya tato vaivāhikaṃ smṛtam vidurāgamanaṃ parva rājyalambhas tathaiva ca
english: Having won her by the law of warriors, the Marriage Parva follows; then the parva of Vidura's arrival, and likewise the parva of the obtaining of the kingdom.

sanskrit: arjunasya vane vāsaḥ subhadrāharaṇaṃ tataḥ subhadrāharaṇād ūrdhvaṃ jñeyaṃ haraṇahārikam
english: The forest sojourn of Arjuna; then the abduction of Subhadrā; after the abduction of Subhadrā comes the parva known as Haranahārika, of gifts for the bride.

sanskrit: tataḥ khāṇḍavadāhākhyaṃ tatraiva mayadarśanam sabhāparva tataḥ proktaṃ mantraparva tataḥ param
english: Then the burning of the Khāṇḍava forest, and within it the appearance of Maya; then the Sabhā Parva is narrated, and after it the Council Parva.

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdhavadhaḥ parva parva digvijayas tathā parva digvijayād ūrdhvaṃ rājasūyikam ucyate
english: The parva of the slaying of Jarāsandha; likewise the Digvijaya Parva of conquest of the quarters; after the Digvijaya, the Rājasūya Parva is spoken.

sanskrit: tataś cārghābhiharaṇaṃ śiśupālavadhas tataḥ dyūtaparva tataḥ proktam anudyūtam ataḥ param
english: Then the offering of the arghya and the slaying of Śiśupāla; the Dice Parva is then narrated, and after it the Subsequent Dice Parva.

sanskrit: tata āraṇyakaṃ parva kirmīravadha eva ca īśvarārjunayor yuddhaṃ parva kairātasaṃjñitam
english: Then the Āraṇyaka Parva, and within it the slaying of Kirmīra; the battle between the Lord Śiva and Arjuna, known as the Kirāta Parva.

sanskrit: indralokābhigamanaṃ parva jñeyam ataḥ param tīrthayātrā tataḥ parva kururājasya dhīmataḥ
english: Next to be known is the parva of the journey to Indra's world; then the pilgrimage parva of the wise king of the Kurus.

sanskrit: jaṭāsuravadhaḥ parva yakṣayuddham ataḥ param tathaivājagaraṃ parva vijñeyaṃ tadanantaram
english: The parva of the slaying of Jaṭāsura; then the combat with the Yakṣa; and right after it is to be known the Ajagara Parva of the great serpent.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeyasamasyā ca parvoktaṃ tadanantaram saṃvādaś ca tataḥ parva draupadīsatyabhāmayoḥ
english: The Mārkaṇḍeya Dialogue Parva is told after that; then the parva of the conversation between Draupadī and Satyabhāmā.

sanskrit: ghoṣayātrā tataḥ parva mṛgasvapnabhayaṃ tataḥ vrīhidrauṇikam ākhyānaṃ tato 'nantaram ucyate
english: Then the Ghoshayatra Parva; then the fear arising from the dream of the deer; then the tale known as Vrihidraounika is narrated immediately after.

sanskrit: draupadīharaṇaṃ parva saindhavena vanāt tataḥ kuṇḍalāharaṇaṃ parva tataḥ param ihocyate
english: The parva of the abduction of Draupadī from the forest by the Sindhu king; then, next here, is told the parva of the theft of the earrings.

sanskrit: āraṇeyaṃ tataḥ parva vairāṭaṃ tadanantaram kīcakānāṃ vadhaḥ parva parva gograhaṇaṃ tataḥ
english: Then the Araneya Parva; immediately after, the Virāṭa Parva; the parva of the slaying of the Kīcakas; and then the parva of the cattle-raid.

sanskrit: abhimanyunā ca vairāṭyāḥ parva vaivāhikaṃ smṛtam udyogaparva vijñeyam ata ūrdhvaṃ mahādbhutam
english: The marriage of Abhimanyu with the princess of Virāṭa is remembered as a parva; from here onward is to be known the great and wondrous Udyoga Parva.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃjayayānākhyaṃ parva jñeyam ataḥ param prajāgaraṃ tataḥ parva dhṛtarāṣṭrasya cintayā
english: Next to be known after that is the parva known as the Journey of Sañjaya; then the Prajagara Parva, arising from Dhṛtarāṣṭra's anxiety.

sanskrit: parva sānatsujātaṃ ca guhyam adhyātmadarśanam yānasaṃdhis tataḥ parva bhagavad yānam eva ca
english: The Sanatsujāta Parva, with its secret vision of the inner self; then the Yamasandhi Parva and the journey of the Lord himself.

sanskrit: jñeyaṃ vivādaparvātra karṇasyāpi mahātmanaḥ niryāṇaṃ parva ca tataḥ kurupāṇḍavasenayoḥ
english: Here is to be known the Vivada Parva concerning also the great-souled Karṇa; and then the parva of the setting out of the Kuru and Pāṇḍava armies.

sanskrit: rathātirathasaṃkhyā ca parvoktaṃ tadanantaram ulūkadūtāgamanaṃ parvāmarṣavivardhanam
english: Then the parva of the enumeration of the great chariot-warriors; then the parva of the arrival of Ulūka as envoy, which heightens the fury.

sanskrit: ambopākhyānam api ca parva jñeyam ataḥ param bhīṣmābhiṣecanaṃ parva jñeyam adbhutakāraṇam
english: Then the Ambā Episode Parva is to be known after this; the Bhīṣma Installation Parva is to be known as wondrous in its cause.

sanskrit: jambūkhaṇḍavinirmāṇaṃ parvoktaṃ tadanantaram bhūmiparva tato jñeyaṃ dvīpavistarakīrtanam
english: The creation of the Jambūdvīpa is told as a parva immediately after; then the Bhūmi Parva is to be known, with its account of the extension of the islands.

sanskrit: parvoktaṃ bhagavadgītā parva bhīṣmavadhas tataḥ droṇābhiṣekaḥ parvoktaṃ saṃśaptakavadhas tataḥ
english: The Bhagavad Gita is told as a parva; then the fall of Bhīṣma; the installation of Droṇa is told as a parva; and then the slaying of the Saṃśaptakas.

sanskrit: abhimanyuvadhaḥ parva pratijñāparva cocyate jayadrathavadhaḥ parva ghaṭotkacavadhas tataḥ
english: The parva of the slaying of Abhimanyu; and the Vow Parva is recounted; the parva of the slaying of Jayadratha; and then the slaying of Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: tato droṇavadhaḥ parva vijñeyaṃ lomaharṣaṇam mokṣo nārāyaṇāstrasya parvānantaram ucyate
english: Then the parva of the slaying of Droṇa, to be known as hair-raising; the release of the Nārāyaṇa weapon is told as the next parva.

sanskrit: karṇaparva tato jñeyaṃ śalyaparva tataḥ param hradapraveśanaṃ parva gadāyuddham ataḥ param
english: Then the Karṇa Parva is to be known; then the Śalya Parva follows; then the parva of entry into the lake; and after it the mace duel.

sanskrit: sārasvataṃ tataḥ parva tīrthavaṃśaguṇānvitam ata ūrdhvaṃ tu bībhatsaṃ parva sauptikam ucyate
english: Then the Sārasvata Parva, endowed with accounts of pilgrimage sites and lineages; above that, the horrific Sauptika Parva is recounted.

sanskrit: aiṣīkaṃ parva nirdiṣṭam ata ūrdhvaṃ sudāruṇam jalapradānikaṃ parva strīparva ca tataḥ param
english: The Aishika Parva is indicated here, exceedingly terrible; then the parva of the water libation; and after that the Stri Parva.

sanskrit: śrāddhaparva tato jñeyaṃ kurūṇām aurdhvadehikam ābhiṣecanikaṃ parva dharmarājasya dhīmataḥ
english: Then is to be known the Śraddhā Parva, the post-mortem rites of the Kurus; then the Installation Parva of the wise king of righteousness.

sanskrit: cārvākanigrahaḥ parva rakṣaso brahmarūpiṇaḥ pravibhāgo gṛhāṇāṃ ca parvoktaṃ tadanantaram
english: The parva of the suppression of Charvaka, the demon in brahmin form; and the distribution of houses is told as a parva immediately after.

sanskrit: śāntiparva tato yatra rājadharmānukīrtanam āpaddharmaś ca parvoktaṃ mokṣadharmas tataḥ param
english: Then the Śānti Parva, where the duties of kings are expounded; the law in times of distress is told as a parva, and after it the law of liberation.

sanskrit: tataḥ parva parijñeyam ānuśāsanikaṃ param svargārohaṇikaṃ parva tato bhīṣmasya dhīmataḥ
english: Then the supreme Anushasanika Parva is fully to be known; then the Svargароhаnika Parva of the wise Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: tato 'śvamedhikaṃ parva sarvapāpapraṇāśanam anugītā tataḥ parva jñeyam adhyātmavācakam
english: Then the Aśvamedha Parva, which destroys all sins; after it the Anugita Parva is to be known, which speaks of the inner self.

sanskrit: parva cāśramavāsākhyaṃ putradarśanam eva ca nāradāgamanaṃ parva tataḥ param ihocyate
english: The parva known as the Forest Hermitage sojourn, and the sight of the sons; then here is told the parva of Nārada's arrival.

sanskrit: mausalaṃ parva ca tato ghoraṃ samanuvarṇyate mahāprasthānikaṃ parva svargārohaṇikaṃ tataḥ
english: Then the terrible Mausala Parva is fully described; then the Mahaprasthana Parva, and after it the Svargarohana Parva.

sanskrit: harivaṃśas tataḥ parva purāṇaṃ khilasaṃjñitam bhaviṣyatparva cāpy uktaṃ khileṣv evādbhutaṃ mahat
english: Then the Harivamsha Parva, a Purāṇa known as a supplement; and the Bhavishya Parva too is told, wondrous and great, also among the supplements.

sanskrit: etat parvaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ vyāsenoktaṃ mahātmanā yathāvat sūtaputreṇa lomaharṣaṇinā punaḥ
english: This full hundred of parvas was spoken by the great-souled Vyāsa, and repeated faithfully by the son of Sūta, Lomaharṣaṇa.

sanskrit: kathitaṃ naimiṣāraṇye parvāṇy aṣṭādaśaiva tu samāso bhāratasyāyaṃ tatroktaḥ parvasaṃgrahaḥ
english: It was narrated in the Naimiṣa forest; the parvas number eighteen in all; this summary of the Bhārata was there set forth as the Parva-Compendium.

sanskrit: pauṣye parvaṇi māhātmyam uttaṅkasyopavarṇitam paulome bhṛguvaṃśasya vistāraḥ parikīrtitaḥ
english: In the Pauṣya Parva the greatness of Utanka is described; in the Pauloma Parva the full expansion of the lineage of Bhṛgu is celebrated.

sanskrit: āstīke sarvanāgānāṃ garuḍasya ca saṃbhavaḥ kṣīrodamathanaṃ caiva janmocchaiḥśravasas tathā
english: In the Āstīka Parva: the birth of all serpents and of Garuḍa; the churning of the milk-ocean; and also the birth of Uccaiḥśravas.

sanskrit: yajataḥ sarpasatreṇa rājñaḥ pārikṣitasya ca katheyam abhinirvṛttā bhāratānāṃ mahātmanām
english: And the story of King Parīkṣit's son performing the serpent sacrifice, through which this tale of the great-souled Bhāratas came to be told.

sanskrit: vividhāḥ saṃbhavā rājñām uktāḥ saṃbhavaparvaṇi anyeṣāṃ caiva viprāṇām ṛṣer dvaipāyanasya ca
english: The various births of kings are told in the Sambhava Parva, and also those of other brahmins and of the sage Dvaipāyana.

sanskrit: aṃśāvataraṇaṃ cātra devānāṃ parikīrtitam daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca yakṣāṇāṃ ca mahaujasām
english: And here is celebrated the descent of portions of the gods, of the daityas, of the danavas, and of the mighty yakshas.

sanskrit: nāgānām atha sarpāṇāṃ gandharvāṇāṃ patatriṇām anyeṣāṃ caiva bhūtānāṃ vividhānāṃ samudbhavaḥ
english: The origins of nagas and serpents, of gandharvas and of birds, and of other diverse beings as well.

sanskrit: vasūnāṃ punar utpattir bhāgīrathyāṃ mahātmanām śaṃtanor veśmani punas teṣāṃ cārohaṇaṃ divi
english: The re-birth of the great-souled Vasus in the Gaṅgā, their residence in Śaṃtanu's house, and their ascent once more to heaven.

sanskrit: tejoṃśānāṃ ca saṃghātād bhīṣmasyāpy atra saṃbhavaḥ rājyān nivartanaṃ caiva brahmacaryavrate sthitiḥ
english: And also here the birth of Bhīṣma through the combined energy of divine portions; his renunciation of the kingdom; and his steadfast vow of celibacy.

sanskrit: pratijñāpālanaṃ caiva rakṣā citrāṅgadasya ca hate citrāṅgade caiva rakṣā bhrātur yavīyasaḥ
english: The keeping of his vow; and the protection of Citrāṅgada; and upon Citrāṅgada's death, the protection of his younger brother.

sanskrit: vicitravīryasya tathā rājye saṃpratipādanam dharmasya nṛṣu saṃbhūtir aṇīmāṇḍavyaśāpajā
english: The installation of Vicitravīrya in the kingdom; and the birth of Dharma among humans, arising from the curse of the sage Aṇimāṇḍavya.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇadvaipāyanāc caiva prasūtir varadānajā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya pāṇḍoś ca pāṇḍavānāṃ ca saṃbhavaḥ
english: And the begetting by Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, born of a boon; the births of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu, and the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: vāraṇāvatayātrā ca mantro duryodhanasya ca vidurasya ca vākyena suruṅgopakramakriyā
english: The journey to Vāraṇāvata; the conspiracy of Duryodhana; and by Vidura's counsel, the construction of the escape tunnel.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānāṃ vane ghore hiḍimbāyāś ca darśanam ghaṭotkacasya cotpattir atraiva parikīrtitā
english: In the terrible forest, the Pāṇḍavas' encounter with Hiḍimba; and the birth of Ghaṭotkaca is celebrated right here.

sanskrit: ajñātacaryā pāṇḍūnāṃ vāso brāhmaṇaveśmani bakasya nidhanaṃ caiva nāgarāṇāṃ ca vismayaḥ
english: The incognito wandering of the Pāṇḍus; their dwelling in a brahmin's house; the death of Baka; and the amazement of the townspeople.

sanskrit: aṅgāraparṇaṃ nirjitya gaṅgākūle 'rjunas tadā bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ sarvaiḥ pāñcālān abhito yayau
english: Having defeated Angarparna on the bank of the Gaṅgā, Arjuna then, together with all his brothers, journeyed toward the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: tāpatyam atha vāsiṣṭham aurvaṃ cākhyānam uttamam pañcendrāṇām upākhyānam atraivādbhutam ucyate
english: Then the Tapatī legend, the Vasiṣṭha legend, and the excellent Aurva legend; the wondrous sub-tale of the five Indras is also told here.

sanskrit: pañcānām ekapatnītve vimarśo drupadasya ca draupadyā devavihito vivāhaś cāpy amānuṣaḥ
english: The deliberation of Drupada regarding the five having one wife; and the divinely ordained, superhuman marriage of Draupadī.

sanskrit: vidurasya ca saṃprāptir darśanaṃ keśavasya ca khāṇḍavaprasthavāsaś ca tathā rājyārdhaśāsanam
english: The arrival of Vidura; the sight of Keśava; and the dwelling at Khāṇḍavaprastha; and likewise the rule over half the kingdom.

sanskrit: nāradasyājñayā caiva draupadyāḥ samayakriyā sundopasundayos tatra upākhyānaṃ prakīrtitam
english: And by Nārada's injunction, the regulation concerning Draupadī; and the sub-tale of Sunda and Upasunda is celebrated there.

sanskrit: pārthasya vanavāsaś ca ulūpyā pathi saṃgamaḥ puṇyatīrthānusaṃyānaṃ babhruvāhanajanma ca
english: The forest sojourn of Pārtha; his meeting on the road with Ulūpī; the journey to holy pilgrimage sites; and the birth of Babhruvāhana.

sanskrit: dvārakāyāṃ subhadrā ca kāmayānena kāminī vāsudevasyānumate prāptā caiva kirīṭinā
english: In Dvārakā, the lovely Subhadrā, enamored of the lover's approach, was won by the diadem-wearer with Vāsudeva's consent.

sanskrit: haraṇaṃ gṛhya saṃprāpte kṛṣṇe devakinandane saṃprāptiś cakradhanuṣoḥ khāṇḍavasya ca dāhanam
english: Taking her away, when Kṛṣṇa the son of Devakī had arrived, the obtaining of the discus and the bow; and the burning of the Khāṇḍava forest.

sanskrit: abhimanyoḥ subhadrāyāṃ janma cottamatejasaḥ mayasya mokṣo jvalanād bhujaṃgasya ca mokṣaṇam maharṣer mandapālasya śārṅgyaṃ tanayasaṃbhavaḥ
english: The birth of Abhimanyu, of supreme radiance, from Subhadrā; the rescue of Maya from the fire; the liberation of the serpent; and the birth of the sharika offspring of the great sage Mandapāla.

sanskrit: ity etad ādhiparvoktaṃ prathamaṃ bahuvistaram adhyāyānāṃ śate dve tu saṃkhyāte paramarṣiṇā aṣṭādaśaiva cādhyāyā vyāsenottamatejasā
english: Thus this first Adi Parva has been told, vast in its scope; it is reckoned by the supreme sage as two hundred chapters, with eighteen additional chapters set down by the radiant Vyāsa.

sanskrit: sapta ślokasahasrāṇi tathā nava śatāni ca ślokāś ca caturāśītir dṛṣṭo grantho mahātmanā
english: Seven thousand shlokas, and nine hundred shlokas, and eighty-four shlokas besides — thus the text was measured by the great-souled one.

sanskrit: dvitīyaṃ tu sabhāparva bahuvṛttāntam ucyate sabhākriyā pāṇḍavānāṃ kiṃkarāṇāṃ ca darśanam
english: The second, the Sabhā Parva, is described as rich in many accounts: the building of the assembly hall by the Pāṇḍavas, and the sight of the servants.

sanskrit: lokapālasabhākhyānaṃ nāradād devadarśanāt rājasūyasya cārambho jarāsaṃdhavadhas tathā
english: The account of the halls of the world-guardians, from Nārada's sight of those divine abodes; the commencement of the Rājasūya; and likewise the slaying of Jarāsandha.

sanskrit: girivraje niruddhānāṃ rājñāṃ kṛṣṇena mokṣaṇam rājasūye 'rghasaṃvāde śiśupālavadhas tathā
english: The liberation by Kṛṣṇa of the kings imprisoned in Girivraja; and at the Rājasūya, during the dispute over the arghya, the slaying of Śiśupāla.

sanskrit: yajñe vibhūtiṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥkhāmarṣānvitasya ca duryodhanasyāvahāso bhīmena ca sabhātale
english: Having seen that splendor of the sacrifice, Duryodhana, seized by grief and indignation, was mocked by Bhīma right there on the floor of the assembly hall.

sanskrit: yatrāsya manyur udbhūto yena dyūtam akārayat yatra dharmasutaṃ dyūte śakuniḥ kitavo 'jayat
english: Where his fury arose, through which he caused the dice game to be played; where the gambler Śakuni defeated the son of Dharma at dice.

sanskrit: yatra dyūtārṇave magnān draupadī naur ivārṇavāt tārayām āsa tāṃs tīrṇāñ jñātvā duryodhano nṛpaḥ punar eva tato dyūte samāhvayata pāṇḍavān
english: Where Draupadī, like a ship on the ocean of dice, rescued them who were drowning; and King Duryodhana, knowing they had crossed over, summoned the Pāṇḍavas once more to the dice game.

sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ sabhāparva samākhyātaṃ mahātmanā adhyāyāḥ saptatir jñeyās tathā dvau cātra saṃkhyayā
english: All this Sabhā Parva has been recounted by the great-souled one; its chapters are to be known as seventy, plus two more in the count.

sanskrit: ślokānāṃ dve sahasre tu pañca ślokaśatāni ca ślokāś caikādaśa jñeyāḥ parvaṇy asmin prakīrtitāḥ
english: Two thousand shlokas, and five hundred shlokas, and eleven shlokas besides — these are to be known as celebrated in this parva.

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu jñeyam āraṇyakaṃ mahat paurānugamanaṃ caiva dharmaputrasya dhīmataḥ
english: After this, the third is to be known as the great Āraṇyaka; and also the following of the citizens after the wise son of Dharma.

sanskrit: vṛṣṇīnām āgamo yatra pāñcālānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ yatra saubhavadhākhyānaṃ kirmīravadha eva ca astrahetor vivāsaś ca pārthasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: Where the Vṛṣṇis come and the Pāñcālas in their entirety; where the tale of the slaying of Saubha is told, and likewise the slaying of Kirmīra; and the exile of the boundlessly radiant Pārtha for the sake of weapons.

sanskrit: mahādevena yuddhaṃ ca kirātavapuṣā saha darśanaṃ lokapālānāṃ svargārohaṇam eva ca
english: The battle with Mahādeva in his guise as a Kirāta hunter; the sight of the world-guardians; and indeed the ascent to heaven.

sanskrit: darśanaṃ bṛhadaśvasya maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ yudhiṣṭhirasya cārtasya vyasane paridevanam
english: The sight of the great sage Bṛhadaśva, whose soul is cultivated; and the lamentation of the afflicted Yudhiṣṭhira in his misfortune.

sanskrit: nalopākhyānam atraiva dharmiṣṭhaṃ karuṇodayam damayantyāḥ sthitir yatra nalasya vyasanāgame
english: The Nala sub-tale right here, righteous and moving to compassion, where Damayantī holds firm during Nala's time of misfortune.

sanskrit: vanavāsagatānāṃ ca pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām svarge pravṛttir ākhyātā lomaśenārjunasya vai
english: And the great-souled Pāṇḍavas, gone into forest exile — their passage to heaven is narrated by Lomaśa to Arjuna.
